title: Setup: a side with no general is the count clause's answer
rationale: Red has a cannon and no general, and the game gives each side exactly one. The count clause carries a floor as well as a ceiling, so this is an answer about the position rather than a refusal to answer about it: the predicate names the side whose complement is wrong and no square, exactly as it does for a side that has too many of a piece. A composing surface reads it as the piece that is still missing.
